questions.q: Using the same $f$ and $g$, find the formula for $(f\circ g)(x)$.
Verify your answer above by computing $f(f^{-1}(5))$.
questions.answer: $f^{-1}(5)=\dfrac{5+2}{3}=\dfrac{7}{3}$, and $f\left(\dfrac{7}{3}\right)=3\left(\dfrac{7}{3}\right)-2=7-2=5$. It matches, confirming the inverse.
Cross-multiply: $2(2x-1)=x+3 \Rightarrow 4x-2=x+3 \Rightarrow 3x=5 \Rightarrow x=\dfrac{5}{3}$ (and $x\neq-3$, so this is valid).
$\dfrac{3}{x-1}=3 \Rightarrow x-1=1 \Rightarrow x=2$ (and $x\neq1$, so this is valid).

questions.q: Given that $x=1$ is a root of $x^3-2x^2-5x+6=0$, use the Factor Theorem to factor completely and find all roots.
questions.answer: By the Factor Theorem, $(x-1)$ is a factor. Dividing gives $x^3-2x^2-5x+6=(x-1)(x^2-x-6)=(x-1)(x-3)(x+2)$. Roots: $x=1,\,3,\,-2$.

questions.answer: Combine: $\log_3\left[(x+2)(x-2)\right]=2 \Rightarrow x^2-4=3^2=9 \Rightarrow x^2=13 \Rightarrow x=\pm\sqrt{13}$. The domain requires $x-2>0$, i.e. $x>2$; since $\sqrt{13}\approx3.61>2$ but $-\sqrt{13}<2$, only $x=\sqrt{13}$ is valid.

questions.q: Given that $x=4$ is a root of $x^3-13x-12=0$, use the Factor Theorem to find the other two roots.
questions.answer: Dividing out $(x-4)$ gives $x^2+4x+3=0$, which factors as $(x-(-1))(x-(-3))=0$, so $x=-1$ or $x=-3$. Answer: $\left(-3,-1\right)$.

questions.q: Given that $x=-6$ is a root of $x^3+13x^2+54x+72=0$, use the Factor Theorem to find the other two roots.
questions.answer: Dividing out $(x+6)$ gives $x^2+7x+12=0$, which factors as $(x-(-3))(x-(-4))=0$, so $x=-3$ or $x=-4$. Answer: $\left(-4,-3\right)$.

questions.q: Given that $x=3$ is a root of $x^3-10x^2+27x-18=0$, use the Factor Theorem to find the other two roots.
questions.answer: Dividing out $(x-3)$ gives $x^2-7x+6=0$, which factors as $(x-1)(x-6)=0$, so $x=1$ or $x=6$. Answer: $\left(1,6\right)$.

questions.q: Given that $x=-3$ is a root of $x^3+2x^2-33x-90=0$, use the Factor Theorem to find the other two roots.
questions.answer: Dividing out $(x+3)$ gives $x^2-x-30=0$, which factors as $(x-6)(x-(-5))=0$, so $x=6$ or $x=-5$. Answer: $\left(-5,6\right)$.

questions.q: Given that $x=2$ is a root of $x^3+6x^2-9x-14=0$, use the Factor Theorem to find the other two roots.
questions.answer: Dividing out $(x-2)$ gives $x^2+8x+7=0$, which factors as $(x-(-7))(x-(-1))=0$, so $x=-7$ or $x=-1$. Answer: $\left(-7,-1\right)$.
